videos.title: Four fields and one clarification habit

slides.title: Make responsibility and output explicit
slides.narration: This short course uses an invented team convention for practice. It is not a policy for your workplace. In Cedar, the owner is the person responsible for the next action. The deliverable is the concrete output. Someone is not an owner. Prepare something is not a useful deliverable. In our supplied case, Maya owns a three-bullet demonstration agenda. Keep those facts separate from assumptions about who else might help.

body: Acceptance: a check someone can perform
slides.title: Make timing and completion observable
slides.narration: Cedar adds a due time with timezone and an observable acceptance check. The supplied agenda is due on 30 October 2026 at 15:00 Asia/Kolkata. Its acceptance check is exactly three bullets: demonstration goal, sequence, and open questions. Soon does not preserve the source date. Looks good does not describe this check. Pause after this slide for two practice questions. Use the supplied facts instead of inventing a different deadline or format.

body: State the three required bullet topics
slides.title: Draft from facts
slides.narration: A complete draft can say: Maya will prepare a three-bullet demonstration agenda by 30 October 2026 at 15:00 Asia/Kolkata. Acceptance means exactly one bullet each for the demonstration goal, sequence, and open questions. Every field comes from the fictional case pack. Writing this draft does not mean Maya has accepted it, the agenda exists, or anyone has received a message. This exercise produces text for review.

body: Record conflicts for the owner to clarify
slides.title: Ask when facts are missing or conflict
slides.narration: For Someone prepare the agenda soon, ask who owns the work, what concrete due time and timezone apply, and how the agenda will be checked. Do not fill the gaps with guesses. In a hypothetical variation, one request says 15:00 and another says 16:00 on the same date. Record both and ask the task owner to clarify. That variation is invented for practice. It does not change the original source case. A draft remains a draft until the relevant people confirm it.

moduleQuiz.title: Check your Cedar handoff decisions
moduleQuiz.instructions: Answer all six questions using the fictional Cedar sources. Questions labelled Select all correct answers require every correct choice and no incorrect choices. The course pass rule is 80%; five of six questions must be correct. Nothing in this quiz sends a message or completes real work.

questions.prompt: Select all correct answers: which fields belong in a complete Cedar handoff?
choices: A named person who owns the next action
A concrete output the owner will produce
A due date, clock time and named timezone
An observable check for the required output
A statement that the output has been sent
questions.hint: Separate required handoff information from claims about completed actions.
questions.explanation: S1 requires owner, deliverable, due time with timezone, and an observable acceptance check. A sent-message claim is not a required field and is not established by a draft (S3).

questions.prompt: Select one answer: which draft preserves every fact in the original agenda case?
choices: Omar owns a three-bullet agenda due 30 October 2026, 15:00 Asia/Kolkata; bullets cover goal, sequence and open questions.
Maya owns a three-bullet agenda due 30 October 2026, 15:00 Asia/Kolkata; bullets cover goal, sequence and open questions.
Maya owns a three-bullet agenda due 30 October 2026, 16:00 Asia/Kolkata; bullets cover goal, sequence and open questions.
Maya owns a three-bullet agenda due 30 October 2026, 15:00 Asia/Kolkata; bullets cover goal, sequence and final invoices.
questions.hint: Compare the owner, deadline and all three bullet topics with S2.
questions.explanation: Only the Maya/15:00/goal-sequence-open-questions option preserves all supplied facts. The other drafts change the owner, clock time or acceptance topics.

questions.prompt: Select all correct answers: what must you clarify in “Someone prepare the agenda soon”?
choices: Which named owner will take responsibility?
Which due date, time and timezone apply?
Which observable acceptance check applies?
Which greeting should accompany the draft?
questions.hint: The case explicitly identifies three missing required details.
questions.explanation: S2 treats the owner, concrete due time/timezone and acceptance check as missing. A preferred greeting is not one of Cedar's four required fields. Ask rather than guess.

questions.prompt: Select one answer: two hypothetical requests give 15:00 and 16:00. What is the appropriate next step?
choices: Keep only 15:00 and describe the earlier time as approved by the owner.
Keep only 16:00 and describe the later time as approved by the owner.
Record both times and ask the task owner which due time should apply.
Remove both times and describe the agenda as already sent to the team.
questions.hint: Do not invent approval, choose a deadline or claim a completed action.
questions.explanation: S3 requires recording both values and asking the task owner to clarify. Neither deadline is automatically approved, and the draft establishes no sent message.

questions.prompt: Select all correct answers: what can you truthfully say immediately after writing a handoff draft?
choices: The draft is available for review and clarification.
The named owner has accepted the work and deadline.
The draft proves neither sending nor completion.
The requested agenda has been finished and shared.
questions.hint: Writing a draft is different from acceptance, sending or completion.
questions.explanation: A draft can be reviewed, but it does not prove acceptance, a sent message, completed work or a shared agenda. Both completion claims are unsupported (S3).

questions.prompt: Select all correct answers: which bullet topics belong in the original agenda acceptance check?
choices: One bullet for the demonstration goal
One bullet for the demonstration sequence
One bullet for the open questions
One bullet for the final project invoice
questions.hint: The original case names exactly three topics, not a generic quality judgement.
questions.explanation: S2 specifies exactly three bullets: goal, sequence and open questions. An invoice is not supplied and adding it would violate the three-bullet acceptance check.

sources.title: Simulated Cedar source S1
sources.reference: SIMULATED SME SOURCE FOR SETUP TEST — fictional training convention, requiring human review. In the fictional Cedar team, a complete handoff states an owner, a concrete deliverable, a due time with timezone, and an observable acceptance check. These are exercise rules, not a real company policy. If a required detail is absent, ask for it instead of guessing.

sources.title: Simulated Cedar source S2
sources.reference: FICTIONAL CASE PACK. Cedar needs a three-bullet demonstration agenda, owned by Maya, due 30 October 2026 at 15:00 Asia/Kolkata. Acceptance check: exactly three bullets, one each for demonstration goal, sequence, and open questions. A second request says only: Someone prepare the agenda soon. Treat its owner, due time and acceptance check as missing.

sources.title: Simulated Cedar source S3
sources.reference: FICTIONAL ESCALATION CONVENTION. When two task requests disagree on a due time, record both values and request clarification from the task owner. Drafting a handoff does not mean the work has been completed or a message has been sent.

miniProject.brief: Build one Cedar handoff pack inside the course: a four-field original-case draft, three clarification questions for the vague request, and an owner-clarification note preserving both hypothetical due times. Use the supplied starter steps to generate and test the three outputs. All cases are fictional; no messages are sent. Allow about seven minutes.
miniProject.title: Your Cedar handoff card - practical sandbox
rubric: All four fields match the original fictional source.
The date, time and timezone are preserved.
No claim that an action was sent or completed.
Both conflicting due times are preserved in the presented order and Maya is asked to clarify.
miniProject.deliverable: One saved and submitted sandbox artifact with complete source-grounded fields and three generated outputs: handoff, clarification and conflict. Both test cases must satisfy the five grading criteria.

instructions: This is one fictional writing-and-simulation project. Produce an original handoff card, a missing-information note, and a conflict note as one submission. Original facts: Maya owns a three-bullet demonstration agenda, due 30 October 2026 at 15:00 Asia/Kolkata; exactly one bullet each covers goal, sequence and open questions. The 16:00 request is a separate hypothetical conflict, not a change to the original case.

Complete all nine artifact fields from the case and S1-S3. The field hints state the observable terms checked by the grader. Write focused questions rather than filling missing facts with guesses. Keep the status as a draft; nothing is sent or completed.

The three starter steps are format scaffolds, not a solution. Leave each operation as template and retain the output names handoff, clarification and conflict. Double-brace references insert your artifact values and the current test input; they do not execute code or contact anyone.

For handoff, enter this format in Expression 1: {{input.label}} | Owner: {{values.owner}} | Deliverable: {{values.deliverable}} | Due: {{values.due}} | Acceptance: {{values.acceptance}} | {{values.status}}
For clarification, enter this format in Expression 2: Request: {{input.vague}} | {{values.askOwner}} {{values.askDue}} {{values.askAcceptance}}
For conflict, enter this format in Expression 3: Due times: {{input.firstDue}}; {{input.secondDue}} | {{values.askConflict}}

Select Run to inspect the draft outputs. Select Test project to check both labelled cases. The second test reverses the two hypothetical due-time inputs: preserve the presented order and ask Maya to clarify instead of choosing a time. Do not hard-code the case label or time sequence into the workflow.

Save draft to retain your work. Fix any failed criteria, then Submit project. All five criteria must pass to enable Continue to final assessment. The automated checks assess the listed facts, required terms and generated outputs; they do not replace human judgement about the quality of your writing. No external environment, account or installation is required. Allow about seven minutes.
